title: Paul M. Romer — Endogenous Technological Change (1990)
use: Nonrival ideas versus rival embodied human capital, excludability and research creation costs; conceptual motivation for the chapter's separately authored innovation law.
verification: Inspected the actual university-hosted original JPE PDF, introduction and section II through printed S76, especially S72–S75 on intentional innovation, rivalry/excludability and the distinction between designs and human skills. The chapter does not reproduce the full Romer equilibrium, its research law, its historical output comparison or empirical parameter estimates. Its bounded proportional law and normalized research-intensity assumption are explicitly original maintained assumptions.

title: Richard R. Nelson and Edmund S. Phelps — Investment in Humans, Technological Diffusion, and Economic Growth (1966)
use: Skills as a channel for adapting to new techniques; distinction between frontier and technology in use, gap-dependent diffusion and limiting relative paths.
verification: Read actual university-hosted original AER paper, printed pp.69–75, including section II hypothesis, both section III models, equations 8–11 of the second continuous-time model and explicit partial-model caveats. Chapter supplies an original exact discrete-time construction with bounded lambda=h/(kappa+h), old-frontier adoption timing, denominator1+g, original parameters and complete boundary/contraction derivation. It does not treat the paper's agricultural association as identified causal evidence or attribute the additive skill-accumulation law to these authors.

title: Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson and James A. Robinson — The Colonial Origins of Comparative Development: An Empirical Investigation (2001)
use: Precisely scoped original empirical identification case: mortality instrument, settlement/institution pathway, dated expropriation proxy and income outcome, relevance and exclusion reasoning.
verification: Inspected actual final AER PDF hosted by MIT, not merely search snippets: introduction printed pp.1370–1371 including the explicit exclusion restriction and disease concern; section IV.B printed pp.1384–1387, equation5, full Table4 panels/header/notes on p.1386 and following interpretation; footnote11 on printed p.1378 and Appendix TableA1 on p.1397 for the private foreign-investment specificity. Verified the baseline64 observations, log PPP GDP per capita1995, protection against expropriation averaged1985–1995 on0–10, and log settler-mortality instrument. No coefficient is imported, no empirical dataset is redistributed or independently reanalyzed, and no claim of checking the paper's complete robustness literature is made. The finite two-world IV example and policy critique are original teaching analysis, not the paper's estimated results.
